title: Product launch video examples: nine 2026 launches to copy
summary: Nine B2B launch videos from 2026, from Asana, Webflow, Linear and more, grouped by launch type, with what each does well.
body_markdown:
TL;DR


- Nine B2B launch videos published between March and November 2026, grouped by launch type, with what each is worth copying.
- They run from 18 seconds to 5 minutes 24 seconds. Five finish under two minutes, and the two longest teach a setup or explain a pricing change.
- Most of the narrated ones name the product within the first 12 seconds and show it inside one concrete situation. Several open on the problem before the product appears.
- Linear and Asana paired a short launch-day video with a longer walkthrough weeks later. The pricing launch explains why before giving numbers, then answers objections.


On April 16, 2026, Linear announced its Microsoft Teams integration with[an 18-second video](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=dailmhIBBUI) and three example messages in the description. On September 10, 2026, Raycast's CEO and co-founder, Thomas Paul Mann, spent[3 minutes 56 seconds on camera](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=FEgUktmN3gs) explaining a pricing change, including answers to the questions people had been asking online. Both videos were launch announcements, and they had very different jobs.


Launch videos have no standard length or format, so the real decision is whether yours has to announce something or explain it. Below are nine launch videos from B2B software companies, sorted by what they launched: a new product, a single feature, an AI feature, an integration, or a pricing change. What to copy from each comes from its captions, description, and launch post.


## What is a product launch video?


A product launch video is a short video a software company publishes on release day to announce a new product, feature, integration, or plan. It shows the new thing working and tells viewers where to get it. A demo video is different, because it teaches a feature people already have.


We cover the workflow from release note to finished video in[how to turn release notes into product launch videos](https://www.clueso.io/blog/how-to-turn-release-notes-into-product-launch-videos) , and demo videos in our[roundup of product video examples](https://www.clueso.io/blog/product-video-examples-we-loved) . This post sticks to launches.

## What do new product launch videos look like?


A new product has to explain itself from zero. One example here narrates every capability, and the other has no narration at all.


**Asana Service Management (September 22, 2026, 1:50).** The narration opens on the problem ("For many businesses, ticketing looks like an endless queue") and names the product at about 12 seconds. Each capability then gets one ordinary request. A password reset is answered on the spot, and an office relocation request turns into a project in one click. The video ends on a URL, and Asana's[general availability post](https://asana.com/inside-asana/asana-service-management) went out the same day.


On October 20, Asana followed it with a 4-minute 56-second[intro walkthrough](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=kJeSlsO00BY) . Copy the pairing of one request with each capability, and save the full tour for a second video.


**Webflow Campaigns (October 20, 2026, 1:31).** YouTube's auto-captions for this film pick up music and no narration, so the description does the explaining. It names the audience (demand gen, growth, and performance marketers) and lays out the workflow in four labelled steps: Plan, Build, Launch, Measure.[Webflow's launch post](https://webflow.com/blog/campaigns-launch) from the same day describes the problem first and places the video after the line "That's why we built Webflow Campaigns." Copy the division of labour, where the film sets the mood and the written copy carries the detail.


## How do software companies launch a single feature on video?


A single feature usually adds a new concept to a product people already know. Both examples here explain that concept before they demo it.


**Linear Releases (May 20, 2026, 2:01).** Linear announced Releases on April 30 with a 30-second[teaser](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=6dIwFoQ0eVg) , then published this narrated walkthrough three weeks later. It defines the new term first ("a set of product changes tracked as issues and bundled together for delivery to users") and explains pipelines before any setup. The demo runs in "our fictional ride-share company workspace," where the narrator sets up an iOS pipeline and follows one issue from in progress to merged to done.


Copy the order: define the noun first, then show it working on invented data that looks real.


**Jira Product Discovery tree views (November 9, 2026, 2:01).** Atlassian announced general availability of the tree view in June, and this video came out in November. It opens on a familiar problem: the link between company goals and day-to-day work "usually lives in someone's head or in a slide deck." The demo then shows the same view twice, once as a leader drilling down from a goal and once as a team tracing its work back up. It closes by naming the plan, Jira Product Discovery Premium.


Copy the two angles, so each kind of user sees the feature from their own seat.


## How do AI feature launch videos explain what the AI does?


AI output changes with every prompt, so a launch video has to show what the feature does in practice.


**Cursor Automations (March 5, 2026, 1:35).** Two members of the Cursor team introduce themselves and say "today, we're launching automations in Cursor" within the first 3 seconds. They explain that the team kept starting agents for the same tasks over and over, then describe automations they run themselves. One triages incidents whenever a PagerDuty monitor goes off, so a likely root cause is waiting before the on-call engineer is fully awake.[Cursor's launch post](https://cursor.com/blog/automations) from the same day lists more examples.


Copy the internal stories, which give viewers a working use case instead of a hypothetical one.


**Framer Skills (September 22, 2026, 0:30).** The video opens with "Your standards shouldn't need repeating," then shows the Framer agent building an about page without skills and calls the result "a good start." The narration explains the difference in one line: prompts tell the agent what to do, and skills tell it how you want things done. It closes by telling viewers to type "skills" to begin. Copy the comparison on one task, starting from a result that is decent but generic, so the feature's contribution is visible.


## How do you show an integration in a launch video?


An integration involves two products, and the viewer needs to see work move between them. These two examples differ in length by more than five minutes.


**Linear for Microsoft Teams (April 16, 2026, 0:18).** YouTube has no captions for this video, so we rely on its description, which gives three example messages, including "@Linear file a bug for this and assign it to me" and "@Linear what's the latest progress on our billing API project?"[Linear's changelog entry](https://linear.app/changelog/2026-04-16-linear-for-microsoft-teams) for that day leads with an 18-second video, the same length as the YouTube upload. Copy the literal commands, because a viewer can paste them into Teams straight away.


**Jira agent in Slack (November 6, 2026, 5:24).** Atlassian announced @Jira in Slack on its[community site](https://community.atlassian.com/forums/Jira-articles/Capture-assign-and-execute-work-in-Jira-from-Slack/ba-p/3252402) in June 2026, and this walkthrough belongs to a later video series. The narrator adds the agent to a channel, turns on comment syncing, and sets one extra instruction: label every work item created from that channel. After creating a work item from the conversation, the narrator posts one Jira comment that syncs to Slack and one that doesn't, then replies from Slack to show it arriving in Jira.


Copy the return trip, and show that the user decides what crosses between the tools.


## How do you announce a new plan or pricing change on video?


A pricing launch asks people to pay, or to pay differently, so the video has to justify the change. We found one qualifying pricing video from the past year.


**Raycast paid plans (September 10, 2026, 3:56).** Thomas Paul Mann starts with the reason. When Raycast launched Pro in 2023, AI was mostly "one question in and an answer out," while agents now call models many times per task, so costs rose and prices didn't. Only then come the numbers: Pro stays at $10 a month, Advanced AI becomes Pro Plus at $20 a month, and a new Max plan sits above both. Existing Advanced AI subscribers move to Pro Plus at their next billing cycle, and the first month of AI usage is doubled for the transition.


The last third is an FAQ that answers objections, including why bringing your own API key now needs a paid plan.[Raycast's announcement post](https://www.raycast.com/blog/changing-how-raycast-ai-is-priced) from the same day embeds the video. Copy the order (reason, numbers, migration, objections), and say what happens to existing customers in the video itself.


## What structure do these launch videos share?


The nine videos range from a music-only film to a five-minute setup walkthrough, but the ones with narration share four habits.


**They name the product early.** Cursor says "launching automations" at 2 seconds, Linear names Releases at 4 seconds, and Asana and both Atlassian videos name their products by 12 seconds. Raycast states the topic, "our new plan and pricing," in the first 6 seconds.


**Several open on the problem.** Asana starts with the endless ticket queue, Atlassian's tree view video with goals that live in someone's head, and Framer with standards that need repeating. Webflow does the same in its launch post, before the video plays.


**One concrete situation carries the demo.** Asana uses a password reset and an office move, and Linear uses an iOS pipeline in a fictional ride-share company. Cursor uses an incident alert, and Framer rebuilds one about page.


**They close on where to get it.** Asana ends on a URL, the tree view video on the Premium plan, and Framer on typing "skills."


Linear and Asana also split announcing from teaching, following a short film with a longer walkthrough weeks later. Raycast split by topic instead, and its pricing video's description points to a separate[AI features video](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ucVSAI2gnro) that went out 12 days later.


## Where do launch videos get used after launch day?


Most of these videos also sit on a page the company owns.[Linear's changelog entry for Releases](https://linear.app/changelog/2026-04-30-releases) opens with a 30-second video, the same length as the YouTube teaser, and the Teams entry opens with its 18-second video. Webflow placed its film inside the launch post, after the problem setup.[Framer's Skills post](https://www.framer.com/blog/skills/) puts the 30-second video directly under the byline, and Raycast's post offers the video to anyone who would "rather watch than read."


Atlassian published both of its videos months after the features shipped, which reaches people who missed the original announcement. You can also put the same file in the in-app "what's new" panel, the release email, a vertical cut for social, and the link a rep sends after a call. We've compared[release-note videos with written changelogs](https://www.clueso.io/blog/release-note-videos-vs-changelogs) if you're unsure whether your changelog needs video.

## Frequently asked questions


### How do you make a product launch video?


Decide whether the video announces the launch or explains it, because that sets the length. Then show the feature working in one situation and end on where to get it. Our guide to[turning release notes into launch videos](https://www.clueso.io/blog/how-to-turn-release-notes-into-product-launch-videos) covers the workflow, and Clueso writes the script and[AI voiceover](https://www.clueso.io/features/ai-voiceovers) for you.


### What should a SaaS product launch video include?


Include the product name, the feature working in a real scenario, who it's for, and how to get it. If the launch involves a plan, name it. The Jira Product Discovery tree view video names the Premium plan before it closes, and Raycast's pricing video says the Pro and Pro Plus prices out loud.


### How do software companies make launch videos without a video team?


Linear's Releases walkthrough and Atlassian's Jira walkthrough each use one narrator talking through the product. Clueso writes the script and voiceover from a rough recording and produces the written guide in the same project, as the[product launch videos page](https://www.clueso.io/use-cases/product-launch-videos) shows.


### How do you write a product launch video script?


Start from the release note, which already says what shipped and who it helps. Open with the product name or the problem it solves, give the demo one scenario, then end on the price or the link. Clueso's AI Rewrite turns rough narration into a polished script on every plan, so you can talk through the feature first and tighten the words afterwards.


### Can you make a product launch video from a template?


Yes. Clueso's[Clueprints](https://www.clueso.io/clueprints) library includes launch templates such as Launch Announcement and Narrated Feature Launch. Clueso's agent asks for your launch details or recording and builds the video in that template's style. Community Clueprints come with every plan, and custom ones with Enterprise.


Before your next release, pick the example from this list that's closest to what you're shipping, and write down the last sentence your video will say, whether that's the price or the link. Then watch the first 10 seconds of that example again and check that your script names the product, or the problem it solves, as early.
